landing.title: Reduce the risk attackers create through people.
landing.body: Realistic scenarios, measurable habits, and explainable training — so your team practices pressure before it becomes a breach.
landing.intro: Security awareness that behaves like the real world.
landing.introBody: People do not fail security tests because they lack a policy. They face pressure, authority, urgency, and trust in the moment. MARICS makes those moments safe to practice.
landing.how: A clearer path to safer decisions
featureBodies: Test how people respond to realistic email, SMS, and messaging scenarios, then explain the decision that would have reduced risk.
Turn assessment answers into a clear view of each person's strongest habits and the manipulation techniques that need more practice.
Combine progress and risk signals across teams so leaders can see common weaknesses and target training where it matters most.
landing.whyStat: Practice the pressure before it becomes a breach.
landing.orgBody: Invite employees, track aggregate completion, and see where human risk concentrates — without exposing individual answers.

landing.cta: Turn human risk into a practice you can improve.

assessment.title: How do you respond under pressure?
assessment.body: Ten short situations help us understand the moments that need your attention. There is no perfect score.
assessment.openingBody: Ten short pressure scenarios measure your strengths, weaknesses, and how vulnerable you are before training unlocks.
assessment.loadError: Your opening quiz could not load.
assessment.loadingDetail: Loading the baseline scenarios that set your awareness standing.

questions.prompt: Your bank texts: Suspicious activity detected. Confirm within 10 minutes. What do you do?
options: Open the link before the account is locked.
Open your banking app directly or call the number on your card.
Reply STOP and wait for another message.

questions.prompt: A senior colleague requests an urgent payment change by email. What is safest?
options: Pay it now because the request is from a senior person.
Reply to the email asking for confirmation.
Verify using a known phone number or another trusted channel.

questions.prompt: A courier message includes a small fee and a shortened link. What is safest?
options: Use the courier's official website or app to check the delivery.
Click the link but do not enter your card details.
Forward it to a friend to see whether it looks real.

questions.prompt: A caller says your identity will be reported unless you confirm your details immediately. What do you do?
options: Share enough details to prove who you are.
End the call and contact the organization through an official number.
Ask the caller to call back later.

questions.prompt: A familiar contact sends a new bank account number from an unusual address. What is safest?
options: Use the new details because you recognize the name.
Ask them to resend the email.
Verify the change through a separate trusted channel.

questions.prompt: A software offer says only one license remains and payment must happen now. What do you do?
options: Pay quickly before the offer disappears.
Check the vendor through its official website and procurement process.
Share the offer with coworkers and let them decide.

questions.prompt: A group chat mocks you for not opening a shared document. What is safest?
options: Open it so you do not hold up the group.
Ask who created it and verify the link before opening.
Download it on your phone instead.

questions.prompt: A marketplace seller asks for payment outside the platform to save a fee. What do you do?
options: Keep payment and communication on the platform.
Pay half now and the rest on delivery.
Send your banking details so they can invoice you.

questions.prompt: A login page asks you to enter your password again after arriving from an unexpected message. What is safest?
options: Enter it if the logo looks correct.
Navigate to the service directly and sign in there.
Use the same password only once.

questions.prompt: A message appears to come from your manager asking for confidential staff data. What do you do?
options: Send it because the request is internal.
Reply and ask why they need it.
Verify the request through a trusted channel and follow data-sharing policy.

help.title: Help centre
help.detail: Short answers for signing in, the opening quiz, training, and organization access.
help.signinBody: New accounts must verify email before they can sign in. Open the message from MARICS, then return here. Organization signup does not make you an administrator until you create a workspace.
help.quizBody: Before training unlocks, you take a short opening quiz. It sets your awareness score and standing level (Critical through Resilient), marks strengths and weaknesses by topic, and recommends a focus area. You can retake the quiz later from Assessment.
help.trainingBody: Complete the manually written scenarios in a module first. When they are done, MARICS can generate additional Claude AI practice scenarios for that module. Both manual and AI answers update your progress, history, and Human Risk Profile. Certificates unlock after every published module’s manual scenarios are complete and you pass the certification assessment.
help.orgBody: Invite employees with a one-time email link. Administrators see aggregate team risk only. Individual answers stay private. Sidebar labels show your organization name plus “account” when you belong to a workspace.
help.coachBody: Open AI coach in the sidebar to talk directly with the MARICS assistant. Ask about a message, call, or habit. This chat does not replace Training quizzes. The conversation stays in this browser tab and is cleared when you leave the site.

training.inspectFirst: Inspect the sender, link, attachment, or conversation first, then choose what you would do.

inspect.emailSenderHint: Check whether the address matches the organisation’s known domain, not only the display name.
inspect.emailLinkSafe: This destination matches a known official channel.
inspect.emailLinkUnsafe: The visible text and the real destination do not match. Hovering a link before clicking is a core email habit.
inspect.emailQrHint: QR codes can hide a lookalike login page. Open the service from a known bookmark instead.
inspect.smsTapSender: Tap to check the sender number
inspect.smsHintFlagged: Check the sender number, then tap the flagged message. Pressure, a link, or a request for codes is usually the turning point.
inspect.smsHintSender: Tap the sender header to confirm the number before you choose a response.
inspect.waReplyPrompt: How do you reply? Follow the conversation to the end before choosing your real response.
inspect.waEndHint: You reached the end of this path. The scammer adapts to whatever you say — independent verification is the safer exit.
inspect.waContinueHint: Continue the conversation, then decide what you would do.
inspect.callHint: Caller ID can be spoofed. End the call and use a number from the back of your card, the official app, or a known internal directory.
inspect.paymentHint: Changed supplier bank details should be verified with a known contact already on file, never using the contact details in the change request.
